place_fields.summary: Abbe Falls is a waterfall on the northeastern side of the Chandradrona range, where a stream descends steeply toward the Bhadra drainage. The site is a less prominent waterfall compared with the better-known Abbey Falls in Kodagu.
place_fields.best_time: Monsoon and post-monsoon months are the most suitable period for waterfall flow; summer conditions can be drier.

planning_attributes.description: Historical regional records describe the Abbe Falls near the northeast side of the Chandradrona mountains as a roughly 600-foot descent by a stream running toward the Bhadra.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: The steep waterfall terrain requires caution; avoid approaching the cascade or wet rock surfaces unnecessarily.
planning_attributes.notes: Do not confuse this Abbe Falls with Abbey Falls near Madikeri in Kodagu.

place_fields.vibe: scenic and spiritually significant mountain waterfall
place_fields.summary: Manikyadhara is a waterfall in the Baba Budangiri hills known for water droplets that resemble a stream of pearls. It is also an important pilgrimage stop associated with both Hindu and Muslim traditions.

planning_attributes.description: Karnataka Tourism describes Manikyadhara as a popular waterfall in the Bababudangiri hills. Access involves descending more than 200 steps, with viewpoints and resting areas along the route.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: The name Manikyadhara means stream of pearls, referring to the appearance of water droplets in sunlight. The site is regarded as holy by pilgrims visiting the nearby Bababudangiri shrines.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: Manikyadhara is about 34 km from Chikmagalur. Regular KSRTC bus service reaches Chikmagalur, from where a taxi can be hired to visit the falls. Kadur Junction is the nearest railway station cited by Karnataka Tourism.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: The approach includes 200+ steps; take care on the stair route, especially when wet.
planning_attributes.notes: Karnataka Tourism lists August to March as the best time and notes that water levels may drop significantly in summer.

place_fields.micro_region: Kemmangundi hills, near Z Point, Chikkamagaluru district
place_fields.vibe: quiet forest waterfall and trekking stop
place_fields.summary: Shanti Falls is a small waterfall on the forested trail to Z Point in Kemmangundi. It is a scenic stop surrounded by Western Ghats vegetation and is commonly combined with the Z Point trek.
place_fields.best_time: Late monsoon and post-monsoon to early winter; July-August gives stronger flow while September-January generally offers clearer trekking conditions.

planning_attributes.description: Shanti Falls lies on the Z Point route in the Kemmangundi hills and forms a natural pool below the cascade. It is surrounded by dense forest and is used as a stop during the trek toward Z Point.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: Reach Kemmangundi and follow the trekking route toward Z Point; Shanti Falls lies en route. Chikmagalur is the nearest major town and can be reached by road, after which visitors can continue by vehicle toward Kemmangundi.
planning_attributes.access_restrictions: The Z Point route is subject to forest/check-post rules and access may be restricted depending on weather or wildlife conditions.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: The trail has narrow and slippery sections, especially during monsoon; use footwear with good grip and take care around the waterfall rocks.
planning_attributes.notes: Shanti Falls is approximately 2 km from Z Point according to local travel references; Karnataka Tourism identifies it as a feature of the Kemmangundi trek.
